## Overview

Fix nine dead external links in the docs. Each one now points at the page's current location.

## Claims

- llm-d integration page: the `kv-management`, `workload-autoscaling` and `flow-control` pages moved to `/docs/architecture/kv-management`, `/docs/operations/autoscaling` and `/docs/operations/traffic/flow-control`.
- Dynamo integration page: `docs/kubernetes/README.md` no longer exists in ai-dynamo/dynamo. The link now goes to the published Kubernetes introduction on docs.nvidia.com.
- TPU links (`.nav.yml`, `features/README.md`, `features/quantization/README.md`): tpu-inference split `recommended_models_features/` into `recommended_models/` and `features/`. The nav entry now points at Recommended Models. The two feature-support notes point at the Feature Matrix, and the quantization one links its `#quantization-support` section.
- `design/metrics.md`: Kubernetes WG Serving was archived, so the link now uses `kubernetes/community/tree/main/archive/wg-serving`.
- `usage/security.md`: the Ray security page moved from `ray-core/security.html` to `ray-security/index.html`.
- `models/extensions/tensorizer.md`: CoreWeave removed its Tensorizer docs page, so the link now goes to the `coreweave/tensorizer` repository.

## Validation

- Ran `lychee --scheme https 'docs/**/*.md'` on main to find the dead links.
- Checked every old URL with `curl -sL` (all return 404) and every new URL (all return 200). I also confirmed that each new page covers the same topic, e.g. the Ray page still states that anyone who can reach the cluster can run arbitrary code.

## Details

Only links are changed, plus the TPU link text where the target page was renamed. I left `deployment/integrations/llamastack.md` alone: Llama Stack is now ogx-ai/ogx and its inline vLLM provider has been removed, so that page needs a content update and not just a link swap.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

AI assistance was used to find and verify these links. I reviewed every changed line.

 [NVIDIA Dynamo](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo) is an open-source framework for distributed LLM inference that can run vLLM on Kubernetes with flexible serving architectures (e.g. aggregated/disaggregated, optional router/planner).
 
-For Kubernetes deployment instructions and examples (including vLLM), see the [Deploying Dynamo on Kubernetes](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/docs/kubernetes/README.md) guide.
+For Kubernetes deployment instructions and examples (including vLLM), see the [Deploying Dynamo on Kubernetes](https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/kubernetes/getting-started/introduction) guide.
 
 Background reading: InfoQ news coverage — [NVIDIA Dynamo simplifies Kubernetes deployment for LLM inference](https://www.infoq.com/news/2025/12/nvidia-dynamo-kubernetes/).

@@ -9,10 +9,10 @@ It is a [CNCF Sandbox project](https://www.cncf.io/blog/2026/03/24/welcome-llm-d
 A single vLLM server is fast, but at scale the picture changes: across many replicas, cache locality breaks under round-robin load balancing, long prompts inflate time-to-first-token, and accelerators sit underused. llm-d adds the cluster-level layer that vLLM does not aim to provide on its own:
 
 - **[Prefix-aware routing](https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/precise-prefix-cache-routing).** Instead of round-robin, llm-d reads vLLM's KV-cache events and routes each request to the replica that already holds its prefix, reusing cache instead of recomputing it.
-- **[Distributed KV-cache management](https://llm-d.ai/docs/architecture/advanced/kv-management).** A global index tracks which token blocks live on which replica, and [tiered offloading](https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/tiered-prefix-cache) spills cache to CPU memory or local SSD, extending the working set beyond accelerator HBM.
+- **[Distributed KV-cache management](https://llm-d.ai/docs/architecture/kv-management).** A global index tracks which token blocks live on which replica, and [tiered offloading](https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/tiered-prefix-cache) spills cache to CPU memory or local SSD, extending the working set beyond accelerator HBM.
 - **[Prefill/decode disaggregation](https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/pd-disaggregation).** Prompt processing and token generation run on separate vLLM workers, with KV-cache moved over the vLLM [NIXL connector](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/nixl_connector_usage/), lowering TTFT and steadying per-token latency on long prompts.
 - **[Wide expert-parallelism](https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/wide-expert-parallelism).** Serve large Mixture-of-Experts models such as DeepSeek-R1 and GPT-OSS across nodes with combined data and expert parallelism, for more KV-cache capacity and throughput.
-- **SLO-aware [autoscaling](https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/workload-autoscaling) and [flow control](https://llm-d.ai/docs/well-lit-paths/foundations/flow-control).** Scale vLLM pools on real inference signals (queue depth, true demand) rather than raw GPU utilization, with multi-tenant fairness and priority dispatch.
+- **SLO-aware [autoscaling](https://llm-d.ai/docs/operations/autoscaling) and [flow control](https://llm-d.ai/docs/operations/traffic/flow-control).** Scale vLLM pools on real inference signals (queue depth, true demand) rather than raw GPU utilization, with multi-tenant fairness and priority dispatch.
 
 These are composable. Most teams start by adding prefix-aware routing over an existing vLLM pool, then layer in the rest as specific bottlenecks appear.

 vLLM model tensors that have been serialized to disk, an HTTP/HTTPS endpoint, or S3 endpoint can be deserialized
